In the quarter Heathfield came away about a furlong from home to score an easy win. The half was rather slow, John Brown striding home as he liked over the last lap.
Heat 2: 1 Heathfield (20); 2 D.

The chief feature of the race was the forward running of several of the younger school, particularly Stan Eeles who perhaps ran his best race to date—Stan has the makings of a real runner if he will get down to it, Fred Clay, John Brown, Bob Boyden, Norman Walker and Alf Heathfield.

In the "Quarter," Heathfield and Freestone were our two runners. Heathfield won his heat in 56.5 secs and although Freestone ran a game race he was unable to get into the placings to enable him to reach the final.

The last event was a four-lap relay race and our team of Underwood, Odde, Heathfield and Picton put up a fine show to win in 2 min. 44.8 secs., which was only a couple of seconds outside the ground record.
Cope was not defending his 440 Senior title and Jim Heathfield proved the new champion with I.

The senior 440 saw Ian Badiali gain a second title in quite fast time, and Jim Heathfield was a good second with Bob Wolton a plucky third. Don Maclean won the junior mile, as expected, and from the way he went off he seemed quite determined to make sure that Geoff Goode had no reserves of speed left.
